n_start: Sarnhold sits at the foot of the spine like a fist on a table, and the thaw has turned its yard to a foot of grey slush. Two of the Compact's nine irons are in the captain's pack, wrapped in salt-cloth, and everybody in the district knows it. The Warden tower, the Reckoning coach and the Sable Guild's loading bay are all in sight of each other, and all three of them are watching the gate.
e_n_start_1: The company rides out of Sarnhold before anybody has laid eyes on it, west and downhill with two irons still in the pack. It is a defensible decision for about four hours. By evening a chartered company that has failed to report to a Commandant is simply five people with stolen Warden property, and it takes one afternoon to become that.
a0_gatehouse: The provost's inspection is thorough because the provost has been told to be thorough. Three irons were expected in the pack and two are found, which the provost writes down twice. A queue of Guild carters waits behind the company for the whole performance, and the charter is read aloud in front of all of them.
a0_gatehouse_a: The irons are declared and sealed under a provost's wax and signed for in a book that the fortress keeps and the Guild reads. It is correct, complete and entirely irreversible. The fortress now knows exactly what the company carries, and so does everybody who was standing in the archway behind it.
a0_gatehouse_b: The charter is presented and nothing at all is volunteered beyond it. The provost reads it three times looking for a reason to be difficult and does not find one, which appears to disappoint him professionally rather than personally. The pack stays shut, and the queue moves on.
a0_gatehouse_c: Nyre answers in the form her order uses, which the provost has to accept and clearly resents accepting. It gets the company through the gate in four minutes. It also puts the Reckoning's name on the company's arrival before the Wardens have theirs, which somebody in the coach yard notes down.
e_a0_gatehouse_1: A chartered company walks past a provost's inspection on its own authority, which the charter arguably permits. The gate crew has been drilled for exactly that eventuality since autumn. The pack is cut off a shoulder in the archway by somebody who knew where the irons were and did not have to look twice for them.
e_a0_gatehouse_2: The provost's seals are demanded back an hour after they were given, which is a confession of second thoughts made in front of eleven witnesses. The charter is suspended pending an inquiry. The inquiry will sit in the spring, and the crown door's nine days will have been over for two months by then.
a0_commandant: Iver Thane has been thirty years on the spine and has read Orr's letter twice. He does not believe the parts of it that are true, which he says out loud, and then asks the only question that matters to him: what does a company of five think it is going to do about a third door. He waits for an answer with his hands flat on the map.
a0_commandant_a: The whole account is given in order across a map table, from Gallowmere to Hollowmarch, and it takes two hours. Thane listens without interrupting once, which is unnerving. At the end he asks for the last part again, with the dates, and writes them into the margin of his own chart.
a0_commandant_b: The account is given the way a soldier gives one: what is shut, what is loose, what is needed and how long there is. It takes eleven minutes. It is the only version Thane can act on before the thaw closes the lower road, and he starts acting on it before the company has left the room.
e_a0_commandant_1: Thane decides, on reflection, that a company carrying two of the Compact's irons is evidence rather than a company. A fortress has cells for evidence and a procedure for holding it. The inquiry is scheduled for when the passes clear, which is nine weeks after the crown door's own schedule runs out.
a0_orders: The orders are short and the charts beside them are not. Eleven lamp stations run up the Ninefold Road to the crown gate of Kar Ashen, and each one has an hour written against it in a hand that is not a Warden hand. A pencil line across the ninth station marks where Thane's last patrol turned back without a written reason.
a0_orders_a: An hour with the charts and a dwarf pathfinder turns eleven stations into eleven questions, and Vurma gets nine of them answered by a man who has walked the road twice. The other two she marks with a circle and says she will answer on the ground. Thane watches the whole exchange and says nothing.
e_a0_orders_1: A Warden column is requested, refused, and minuted. Thane has four hundred men for two hundred miles of spine and a written reason for the placement of every one of them. The company stands in a map room being thanked for its service, which is what a refusal sounds like when it is delivered properly.
a0_armoury: The quartermaster has been told to be generous and is not enjoying it. Crampons, spine rope, pitch, forty dwarf candles, a moor-iron pick and a warded haft come out onto the counter, and the haft has a Warden's initials filed off the ferrule. He does not explain the haft, and he books it out looking at the wall.
a0_armoury_a: Spine rope, crampons and forty candles, signed for in triplicate by a man who counts them twice. It is the least interesting transaction in Sarnhold. It is also the difference between the ice gallery being a route and being a paragraph in somebody's report next spring.
a0_armoury_b: A moor-iron pick and a warded haft come off the back rack, both cold in the hand in the way that ordinary iron is not. The quartermaster books them out without meeting anybody's eye. Ilsabet turns the haft over twice and says that whoever warded it knew exactly what it would be used against.
e_a0_armoury_1: Everything is drawn and nothing is signed for, on the reasonable grounds that there is no time. The quartermaster swears his complaint before the provost within the hour. The charter survives the accusation and does not survive the delay, because the crown door is nine days off and the hearing is eleven.
a0_legate: Prior Absolon Rell has come up from the mother house with a coach, four novices and a writ already drawn. He wants the two irons placed in the Reckoning's custody today, for safekeeping, and he has a receipt prepared with the company's names already entered on it in a clerk's hand. He is polite, and he is not in any hurry at all.
a0_legate_a: The writ is read out in full in a cold chapel with the company standing. Custody, safekeeping, indemnity, and then a clause about the count that Nyre stops him in the middle of, because she has read it twice already and can quote the rest of it from memory. Rell lets her finish, and then continues from where she stopped.
a0_legate_b: The refusal is given plainly to a mother-house legate in front of four novices: the irons are Warden property and will be handed to a Warden. It costs the company its welcome in the chapter house before supper. By evening it has bought the company something with Thane that no amount of paperwork would have.
e_a0_legate_1: The legate's escort is four novices and a receipt, which turns out to be enough. Two irons go into a coach with the Reckoning's seal on the door, properly signed for. The company stands in a fortress yard holding a piece of paper, three books of leverage lighter, watching southern horses turn out of the gate.
a0_chapel: Sarnhold's chapel has a tally on its east wall in groups of nine that nobody in the fortress can account for. The chaplain has been counting them for six years as a devotional exercise and has never once asked what the count is of. He offers to show the company the wall the way a man offers to show visitors a garden.
a0_chapel_a: The east wall reads as nine hundred years of groups, cut by many hands, in the same system the company has now seen at Kar Duhn, Sixteen Mile and every gibbet post in between. The last group has eight strokes cut and a ninth begun. The mortar dust of the ninth stroke is still on the flagstones underneath it.
e_a0_chapel_1: The chaplain is asked the question he has spent six years not asking, in front of his own congregation, and he answers it. Then he rings the bell. It empties the chapel in ninety seconds and fills the provost's office instead, and the company spends the evening explaining a charter rather than reading a wall.
a0_relics: The chapel reliquary holds three tally-irons on velvet under glass, labelled as relics of the founding and dated to the legion. There is a fourth setting with its label already in place and nothing on the velvet. The label has a date on it, and the date is this spring.
a0_relics_a: One tally-iron comes off the velvet, and it is cold as well-water and heavier than any relic has business being. The reliquary now has two empty settings in a row, which somebody will notice at the evening office. Ilsabet puts the iron in her own pack and starts, quietly, sorting the company's irons by gauge.
a0_relics_b: Four labels read in a chaplain's careful hand; three name founding wardens with dates nine hundred years back. The fourth names nobody at all: it has an office, a term of nine years, and a date this spring, and the copperplate is fresh enough that the burr is still on the letters.
e_a0_relics_1: The glass is broken in a Warden chapel to settle a question about a label. The answer arrives from the direction of the empty setting rather than from the glass, and it uses the captain's own name and the correct rank. Afterwards the fourth setting is no longer empty, and the label has been filled in.
a0_novices: Rell's four juniors sleep in a dormitory off the chapter house, and somebody has set out a jug of hot wine for the company's arrival, and four cups are poured; a fifth stands beside the jug, dry, with its own napkin. Two of the novices will not look at the tray at all.
a0_novices_a: The wine is refused, out loud, with the reason given, and four novices look relieved rather than insulted. One of them follows the company into the corridor to say four words about the fifth cup, and then goes back inside before anybody can ask him a fifth. Nyre writes the four words down.
a0_novices_b: The wine is drunk, and it is good wine; the night that follows is eleven hours of sleep nobody chose to take. In the morning the kit has been gone through with real care, and the provost's seals on the pack have been broken and re-set by somebody with the patience to match the wax.
e_a0_novices_1: The jug goes out of a dormitory window in front of four novices of the mother house, which is satisfying for about nine seconds. Rell's complaint reaches the provost before the wine reaches the yard below. The charter is suspended for the length of an inquiry into conduct, and the inquiry is in no hurry.
a0_guildhall: Bruk Sunder has a contract drawn before the company sits down. The Sable Guild will underwrite the whole expedition: kit, hands, provisions, a train as far as the fourth station. In exchange it wants the charts, the hours, and first claim on the crown road afterwards, and it has already had the clauses witnessed.
a0_guildhall_a: The offer is heard out in full, which takes a quarter of an hour and includes three concessions Sunder did not have to make. That is the interesting part. A Guild factor who gives away three points unprompted is a factor who already knows what is up that road and has costed it.
a0_guildhall_b: The refusal is given across a guildhall table: the road is not the company's to sell. Sunder takes it well, thanks the captain for the clarity, and has his clerk minute the exchange. Taking it well is worse than taking it badly, because it means he has a second plan and has had it for some time.
e_a0_guildhall_1: The underwriting is signed and the Guild's money lands the same afternoon, which solves every practical problem the company has. A delving train is on the road inside the week with the company's own charts in its wagon-master's satchel. The charter's authority, from that morning on, belongs to whoever holds the paper.
a0_charts: The Guild chart room holds three surveys of the crown road that the Wardens do not have; two are old. The third is dated this spring and initialled by a surveyor whose name is on the Guild's own missing list, and it shows the crown gate closed and two ways into the outer ward that no Warden chart records.
a0_charts_a: An hour of copying in Ilsabet's shorthand with Vurma reading elevations aloud beside her. The spring survey comes away as nine pages of the company's own. It shows a foundry chimney and a cistern channel, both of them entering the ward under its wall, and a note about the ninth hour in the surveyor's hand.
e_a0_charts_1: The spring survey comes off the guildhall wall entire, which is faster than copying and leaves a rectangle of clean plaster. It is missed within the hour. The Guild's grievance at the provost's desk ends with the company's charts impounded as disputed property and the charter under review by supper.
a0_forge: The Guild forge is still hot at the ninth hour and the smith will cut anything for coin. She does not ask why a surface company wants a blank in the founding gauge, or what the two wrapped objects in the pack are, or why one of them is being measured against her own gauge plates while she works.
a0_forge_a: A blank cut to the founding gauge, filed true and wrapped in salt-cloth, for eleven crowns. Ilsabet stows it herself. It is either the most useful object in the company's baggage or the single most damning thing in it, and which of those it turns out to be depends entirely on what happens at the crown door.
a0_forge_b: The pick is re-tempered and the warded haft is rewarded properly for the first time since Gallowmere, which costs a day's fee and most of an evening. The company gets both back better than they went in. In the first ice gallery above the fourth station, that evening pays for itself twice.
e_a0_forge_1: Two of the Compact's irons are handed to a Guild smith to be copied, and copies are made, and originals are handed back. Nobody in the company can say afterwards, with any certainty at all, which pair went into the pack and which pair stayed in Sarnhold. Neither can anybody else, which is the point.
a0_delvers: The delvers' yard has four Sable Guild hands in it with opinions about surface companies holding dwarf irons. They are not keeping the opinions to themselves. Two of them recognise Vurma Kell as the pathfinder whose report their own foreman burned last spring, and the recognition does not improve anybody's temper.
a0_delvers_a: Four exchanges, a broken trestle, and a delver sitting down hard in the slush with his opinion substantially revised. The yard foreman calls it fair in front of everybody, because the alternative is the provost. Dellach's hand is split again, and Nyre binds it without comment, which is her way of commenting.
a0_delvers_b: A cask is bought and Vurma is given the floor for eleven minutes, which is all she needs; by the end of it the yard knows exactly what its own foreman burned last spring and why. Two of the four will not look at him again, and one of them says so out loud in front of the others.
a0_delvers_c: The Guild's founding oath is recited back to the yard in dwarf by a hedge-thaumaturge with a southern accent, correctly, including the clause about surveys. The yard stops dead. Ten minutes later the company has a guide it did not ask for and did not pay for, standing at the gate with her own kit.
e_a0_delvers_1: Steel drawn in a Guild yard inside a Warden fortress engages two jurisdictions at once, and both of them respond. The company is in the provost's cells by the ninth hour with its charter impounded and its irons in a strongbox, and the Guild's complaint and the provost's charge sheet arrive at Thane's desk together.
e_a0_delvers_2: A yard fight pressed past the point where it was won turns four delvers into a Guild grievance, and a Guild grievance into a knife under a rib in a slush-filled yard that nobody was watching. It takes about four seconds. The Ninth Sword loses its captain forty miles from the road it came to walk.
a0_market: The thaw market is mud to the ankle and the whole spine is selling what it has: rope, salt beef, dwarf candles, crampons, a stall of tally-irons labelled as scrap. A boy is selling lamp oil by the ninth rather than by the pint. That is not a measure anybody uses on the frontier, and nobody at the market finds it odd.
a0_market_a: Nine tally-irons bought as scrap at the price of scrap, four of them founding gauge; Ilsabet spreads them on a bunkroom bed that night and sorts them into two piles without explaining either pile. In the morning one pile is in her pack and the other is back at the stall, sold on.
a0_market_b: A month of salt, oil and beef, loaded on the barrow and lashed down. It is the least interesting purchase anybody makes in Sarnhold and the one that decides how the ice gallery goes. Halt and Weem take the handles in turns and complain in alternation the whole way up the first switchback.
e_a0_market_1: The boy is asked who taught him to sell oil by the ninth, and he answers honestly, because he is nine and has no reason not to. The two men who have been standing behind his stall all morning decide the question is worth following up, and they follow it up in an alley off the market before dark.
a0_taproom: The Hooked Lamp is full of Guild carters and off-duty Wardens, and one table of Rooks in charter colours. The story of Kar Duhn is being told at the bar by three people who were not there, badly, with the names wrong. It is the fourth time this month, and it has improved with each telling in every way except accuracy.
a0_taproom_a: The story is corrected with names, dates and the actual sequence, by somebody who was standing in the room when it happened. The bar does not enjoy it. The correction reaches Thane's clerk before the company reaches the door, and it reaches Corrow's people at their own table in about nine seconds.
a0_taproom_b: A round is bought and the bad version is left standing, which costs four crowns and buys the room's goodwill. It is the first entirely sensible thing anybody in the company has done in Sarnhold. The version being told gets worse over the evening and nobody in the Ninth Sword corrects a word of it.
e_a0_taproom_1: An argument about Kar Duhn becomes an argument about the irons, in a room with a Rooks table in it and a pack on the floor under a bench. The company wakes in the provost's cells. The pack has been inventoried in somebody else's handwriting, and two entries on the list are ones nobody in the company recognises.
a0_brawl: The Rooks lieutenant was at Hollowmarch and lost four people there, and he wants the company to explain, out loud, in front of the room, whose orders those four died under; it is a fair question asked in an unfair place. The room goes quiet enough to hear the fire, and Dellach puts his cup down flat.
a0_brawl_a: A yard fight against a man with a real grievance, which is the worst kind to win. The company wins it on points and loses it in every other respect, and the lieutenant goes down twice and gets up twice. Nyre binds two sets of knuckles afterwards and says nothing at all about either of them.
a0_brawl_b: The question is answered honestly in front of a full room: whose orders, what those orders were, what the company learned, and what it did with what it learned. It takes four minutes. The lieutenant listens to all of it, says one sentence at the end of it, and goes back to his own table.
a0_brawl_c: Four dead are named aloud with a round bought for each, in the old free-company form that predates the Rooks and the Wardens both. The lieutenant accepts it because there is no version of him that could refuse it. Both companies drink standing, and afterwards nobody in the room raises Hollowmarch again.
e_a0_brawl_1: The grievance is sent up to Corrow rather than settled in the room, which is procedurally correct. Corrow arrives in Sarnhold two days later with a chartered company and a written complaint. The inquiry that follows keeps everybody off the spine until the passes close, which suits exactly one of the parties.
e_a0_brawl_2: A yard fight is continued past the point of decision, in slush, in front of Wardens. The Rooks lieutenant does not get up the third time. A provost has no discretion at all in the matter of a killing inside a fortress, and the charter, the irons and the company's whole purpose end in the same hour.
a0_bunks: The fortress bunkroom is warm from the kitchen flue, the door bars from inside, and the pack goes under the captain's head; there is a whole night available for the first time since the Deep Road. Outside, the spine stands over Sarnhold with the Ninefold Road on it as a thread of lamps going up into cloud.
a0_bunks_a: One whole night on a straw mattress in a warm stone room with the door barred and no watch kept, which everybody in the company has learned the value of the hard way; nobody dreams about counting. In the morning five people pick up their kit like people who intend to come back for the rest of it.
a0_roster: The company is two hands short since Hollowmarch and there are forty applicants in the yard, because Sarnhold is a fortress town in a thaw and work is work. At the front of them is Ossa Vend's cousin Mira with her own lighting pole, and behind her a Warden veteran called Hask who has been up the road twice.
a0_roster_a: Mira Vend is hired at a half share with her own pole, and Hask at a full one because he has been up the Ninefold Road twice and does not pretend to have enjoyed either trip. Both of them ask about the hours before they ask about the money, which is the only qualification that matters.
a0_roster_b: Forty applicants are refused in one sentence each, which takes an hour and is the correct decision. Five people who have survived two doors together do not need two strangers learning the count on the ice stair. The company goes up the spine at exactly the strength that came down off Hollowmarch.
e_a0_roster_1: A hiring yard worked through carelessly at the end of a long day. One of the forty turns out to be a Reckoning novice under instruction with a writ folded in his boot. The company discovers the writ above the ice gallery rather than in the yard, which is nine days too late and four thousand feet too high.
a0_kit: The company's kit is spread on a fortress floor for the first honest inventory since Gallowmere. Two irons in salt-cloth, three books, a bag of tally-die fragments, and rope that has been up two mountains too many. Written out on a slate, it is a strange list for a chartered company and a very clear one for an inquiry.
a0_kit_a: New spine rope, two clean reservoirs and a spare wick roll, for eleven crowns. It is a boring purchase. In the crevasse above the ice stair it is the difference between a crossing and a paragraph, which is a sentence Vurma says out loud while she coils the new rope and which nobody argues with.
a0_kit_b: The two irons are split between two packs on Ilsabet's insistence, which halves what a single theft can take and doubles the number of people who can be robbed. She argues for it anyway, on the grounds that the second risk is a fight and the first is simply an ending, and the company agrees with her.
e_a0_kit_1: One iron is left in the fortress strongbox for safekeeping, receipted properly, with two Wardens on the door. On the ninth night the strongbox is opened by two Wardens whose cloaks do not fit them. In the morning the receipt is the only iron the Ninth Sword owns, and receipts do not fit sockets.
a0_night: The last night in Sarnhold, and the spine stands over the fortress in moonlight with the Ninefold Road visible on it as a thread of lamps going up into cloud; you can count nine of them from the wall. The ninth is the highest, and it is lit two hours before any chart in the fortress says it should be.
a0_night_a: A full night's sleep taken deliberately by five people who have learned what not taking one costs. Nobody sits up with the charts. In the morning everybody's hands work, which sounds like nothing and is the difference between the ice stair and the bottom of it.
a0_council: The company council is held in a fortress stable because it is the only room nobody else wants. The question is how the Ninth Sword goes up a road with eleven counted stations on it and a closed gate at the top, and every option on the table is bad in a different direction.
a0_council_a: The decision is to go up openly on the charter, station by station, signing the book at each one. It is slow, it is legal, and it gives the road nine days' notice of the company's arrival. Dellach argues for it on the grounds that the alternative is arriving somewhere as smugglers, and he is not wrong.
a0_council_b: The decision is to go up inside the Guild train as carters, which puts forty witnesses around the company and forty pairs of hands within reach of the packs. Kettle argues for it and does not pretend to like the second half of it. Ilsabet's only condition is that the irons travel on her back and not on a wagon.
a0_council_c: The decision is to split the company one day apart, which is what Thane would advise and what nobody in the room likes. It halves what a single ambush takes and it means somebody walks the ice gallery without Ossa. The argument about which half goes first runs for a quarter of an hour and settles nothing.
e_a0_council_1: The council runs until the Guild train has gone, the weather has turned, and the crown door's nine days have become four. Nobody makes a bad decision. Nobody makes any decision, which is worse, and the company is still arguing in a stable when the ninth station's lamps are lit for the last time that matters.
e_a0_council_2: Word is sent ahead to eleven counted stations that a chartered company is coming up on the charter, station by station, which is courteous and correct. It is read at the fourth station by exactly the wrong clerk. By the time the company reaches the third station, everything above it has had four days' notice.
a0_stables: There are no horses for the spine above the fourth station and the stables know it. What is available is one hand-barrow with a broken shaft, two mules on hire, and a place on the Guild train loading in the next yard. The Guild's fourth wagon is loaded with sealed crates and the wagon-master will not discuss its manifest.
a0_stables_a: The barrow shaft is mended with a spliced ash haft and wire in an hour, and Vurma pronounces the repair better than the original in the tone she uses for things she intends to be asked about later. It carries four hundred pounds up nine switchbacks without complaint, which is more than the porters manage.
a0_stables_b: Two mules hired as far as the fourth station, with a boy to bring them back down. It buys the company four days of not carrying and costs it four days of not being quiet, because a mule on dwarf paving can be heard from a station away and both of these have opinions.
e_a0_stables_1: A place is taken on the Guild train, which is warm, fed and fast. At the second station the fourth wagon's load shifts and one crate's seal splits, and the company sees what it has been helping to haul up a mountain. The wagon-master's account of the discovery, given later, does not mention the company at all.
a0_wagons: The Guild train is loading for the crown road: eleven wagons, forty hands, and a wagon-master who cannot account for the fourth wagon's manifest and has stopped pretending to try. He is not lying. He simply has a bill of lading that lists weights against nine entries and no description against any of them.
a0_wagons_a: The manifest is read line by line by a Reckoning sister who has spent two books learning what to look for. Nine entries in a hand she has now seen in three fortresses. One entry with no weight recorded against it at all, which in a Guild manifest is not an omission but a category.
a0_wagons_b: The fourth wagon's seal is broken in a loading yard in front of forty Guild hands, which costs a fight, a fine and the Guild's cooperation for the whole spine. Inside are nine crates of founding-gauge blanks packed in chaff. The fine is eleven crowns and the company pays it in the yard, in coin, without arguing.
e_a0_wagons_1: Guild business is left to the Guild, which is defensible, and the fourth wagon goes up the Ninefold Road a day ahead of the company. Everything that happens at the fourth station afterwards happens because of what was in it. The company reads about the first part of it in a station book and walks into the rest.
a0_scouts: Thane's three road scouts are in the map room because there is nowhere else in Sarnhold they are allowed to be; between them they have walked to the ninth station and back this year. None of them will go past it for any money the Wardens have, and all three of them say so in the same words.
a0_scouts_a: The ninth station described by three people who have stood in it: lamps lit two hours early, a count that runs backwards, and a station book signed every single day since autumn in the same hand; none of them saw who signs it. All three of them looked, which is why none of them will go back.
a0_scouts_b: The way in that is not the gate, given reluctantly and drawn on a slate: the foundry chimney at the outer wall, ninety feet, staples at the bends, coming out in the ward's slag yard. The oldest scout adds a warning about the ninth hour and then rubs the slate clean with his sleeve before anybody can copy it twice.
e_a0_scouts_1: A scout is pressed for a route he has already refused twice, in front of his own officer, and he gives it up. The company gets the route. It also gets a Warden complaint that reaches the provost by evening, because a man who has been broken in front of his officer will find a way to be heard.
a0_farewell: The last hour before the road goes on the free-company custom that has never once been optional: letters written and left with a fortress clerk against the company's return. There is a book for it. It has four hundred letters in it, and eleven of them have been collected by the people who wrote them.
a0_farewell_a: Five letters written in a fortress hall and handed to a clerk, sealed, dated and entered in the book. Nobody reads anybody else's. Dellach's takes the longest, Kettle's takes four lines, and Ilsabet writes two and hands over both, which nobody comments on and everybody notices.
e_a0_farewell_1: One letter is written and read aloud to the company in a fortress hall, which is not the custom and cannot be undone. It is well written, which makes it worse. Five people go up the Ninefold Road the following morning already grieving themselves, and morale does not survive the third station.
a0_road: First light at the foot of the Ninefold Road, and the spine stands over Sarnhold in cloud with eleven counted stations above and a crown gate at the top of them; the road itself is dwarf paving nine feet wide, in good order, swept. Three ways go up from this first switchback, and the company has to pick one now.
